visual.general_description: Black-and-white tree diagram of grey boxes joined by plain lines, classifying hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis by blood pressure, renin and aldosterone, and by genetic versus acquired cause.
visual.detailed_description: A single box on the far left reads "Hypokalemic Metabolic alkalosis" in vertical text and branches into two boxes: "With normal or low blood pressure" and "With high blood pressure". The first branches into "Renal losses of sodium chloride" and "Extrarenal losses of sodium chloride", each splitting into "Genetic Diseases" and "Acquired diseases" boxes. Renal losses lead to "Bartter and Gitelman syndromes" and "East syndrome" (genetic) and "Diuretic use" (acquired); extrarenal losses lead to "Congenital chloride diarrhea" and "Cystic fibrosis" (genetic) and "Vomiting" (acquired). The high blood pressure branch splits into "With low renin and aldosterone", "With low renin and high aldosterone" and "With high renin and aldosterone". The first leads to genetic "Apparent mineralocorticoid excess" and "Liddle and Geller syndromes" and acquired "Cushing syndrome" and "Licorice abuse"; the second to genetic "Familial Hyperaldosteronism"; the third to "Acquired or genetic of causes of Renal artery stenosis" and "Renin secreting tumor". The connectors are plain elbow lines without arrowheads.

visual.general_description: Pedigree with open and filled symbols and three pairs of Sanger sequencing traces labelled Mother, Father and Index case.
visual.detailed_description: Whole figure combines Sanger chromatograms with a pedigree. The word "Mother" is printed at the top left and "Father" at the top right, each above a pair of stacked chromatogram traces with a header text line above each trace and a row of base-call letters below it; in each of these, one letter is highlighted in a black box. In the centre is a pedigree: an open circle on the left joined by a horizontal line to an open square on the right, a vertical line down to a sibship line, and below it an open square and a solid black circle. The word "Index case" is printed at the bottom centre under a further pair of stacked chromatogram traces with the same layout. The traces for the parents show base-call letters including repeated "N" entries beside the highlighted letter, and the index case traces show a continuous series of letters without "N" entries.
